title: What a Number-Guessing Game Teaches About Binary Search and Vue State
summary:
A higher-or-lower number game can give misleading hints or attempt counts if the secret and round state change at the wrong time. I'll use a small Vue implementation to show how to keep those updates consistent, then explain why midpoint guesses put a worst-case bound on the number of attempts.

The player chooses a range, submits a number, and gets a high, low, or correct result. There is no computer player performing binary search. The useful connection is that the feedback gives a human player exactly the information needed to shrink a search interval.

title: Japan Leaked 1.6 Million Driver's License Photos. What AI Changes
summary:
Japan just leaked about 1.6 million photos of driver's licenses.
And in the age of AI, a photo of your ID is exactly what a scammer wants.

I've run a web platform in Tokyo for 22 years. Keeping member data safe is the part of my job that keeps me up at night.
So I read every official notice from the company in Japanese, all five of them, and the bank announcements that followed.
I made a video about it too. This article has the numbers the video couldn't hold: the final count, how long the photos were kept, which banks stopped accepting ID photos and when, and how the chip check actually works.

title: Your IP is on a blocklist: how to check it in 5 minutes and what actually gets you delisted
summary:
Mail starts bouncing, a partner's firewall stops answering, or a website shows your server a captcha wall. Someone says "your IP is blacklisted", and the first instinct is to ask for a new one. Usually that's the wrong first step. Here's how to find out what's actually going on, in about five minutes, and what fixes it for good.

What a "blocklist" actually is

The word covers three different things, and they're fixed in different ways.

  1. DNS blocklists (DNSBLs). Public lists of addresses that sent spam or showed signs of compromise. Mail servers query them for every incoming connection. This is what "blacklisted" usually means, and it's the fixable kind.
  2. Private reputation at big mailbox providers. Large webmail services keep their own scores and don't publish them. You see the effect (mail lands in spam or is deferred) but there's no list to check, only their postmaster tools.

title: Battery date codes: why K5 can mean three different months
summary:
What does the date code on a car battery mean? On most brands it's a letter for the month and a digit for the year, so C3 means March 2023. That's Interstate's own example, and it sounds like a five-minute regex.

Then you read the same code across brands. K5 is November 2025 on an Interstate. On a Deka it's October 2025. On a NorthStar it's September 2025.

Same two characters, three different months, and that's before you get to the missing decade.

I built a battery date code decoder that covers 13 brands, 10 of them with a rule from the maker. This post covers the parsing problems I hit, and how the decoder handles a code it can't settle. The rules are open data, so you can use them yourself.

title: Discord webhook in a contact form? Anyone can delete it
summary:
A Discord webhook URL looks like an address, so it feels fine to put it in your page's JavaScript. It works more like a key. Discord's developer docs list three calls that need nothing but that URL: Get Webhook with Token, Modify Webhook with Token and Delete Webhook with Token. Each one "does not require authentication." So anyone who opens your page source can post to your channel, rename the webhook and give it a new avatar, or delete it. Once it's deleted your form stops delivering, and you find out when a customer asks why you never answered.

That's the whole problem. The rest of this piece is how common it is and how to fix it.

We're Formgong, and we make a form backend that posts to Discord. Our product is in the last section, and you can skip it.
